FEDERAL CORPORATE TRANSPARENCY ACT / BENEFICIAL OWNERSHIP INFORMATION REPORTING — INFORMATION SHEET
Prepared for Acme, Inc.

ABOUT THIS INFORMATION SHEET
This information sheet describes the federal beneficial ownership information ("BOI") reporting regime created by the Corporate Transparency Act (CTA), codified at 31 U.S.C. § 5336, and implemented by the U.S. Department of the Treasury's Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FinCEN) at 31 C.F.R. § 1010.380. It reflects the scope of that regime as revised by FinCEN rulemaking effective March 26, 2025 and made permanent by a final rule effective August 14, 2026. This is a federal reporting obligation separate from any California filing. This document states the regulatory text as fetched and independently verified on the date checked above; it does not determine whether Acme, Inc. currently has a reporting obligation, which depends on facts about its jurisdiction of formation and the citizenship or residency of its owners.

STATUTORY DEFINITION OF "REPORTING COMPANY"
The Corporate Transparency Act, as codified at 31 U.S.C. § 5336(a)(11), defines a "reporting company" as a corporation, limited liability company, or other similar entity that either (i) is created by filing a document with a secretary of state or similar office under the law of a State or Indian Tribe, or (ii) is formed under the law of a foreign country and registered to do business in the United States by such a filing. This statutory definition has not been amended since enactment; the current, narrower scope of who must actually report is instead the product of implementing regulations described in a separate authority clause below.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-06]
  "(11) Reporting company .-The term "reporting company"- (A) means a corporation, limited liability company, or other similar entity that is- (i) created by the filing of a document with a secretary of state or a similar office under the law of a State or Indian Tribe; or (ii) formed under the law of a foreign country and registered to do business in the United States by the filing of a document with a secretary of state or a similar office under the laws of a State or Indian Tribe"
  — 31 U.S.C. § 5336(a)(11)(A) — Corporate Transparency Act, beneficial ownership information reporting requirements, 31 U.S.C. § 5336(a)(11)(A) (https://uscode.house.gov/view.xhtml?req=granuleid:USC-prelim-title31-section5336&num=0&edition=prelim)
  Known gap: This clause states the statute's own definition, which by its terms would include domestic (U.S.-formed) entities. It does not by itself describe the current, narrower regulatory scope -- the implementing regulation, addressed in this document's next clause, currently excludes all domestic entities from reporting-company status. Reading this clause alone, without the next one, would give an inaccurate picture of who currently must report.

2025-2026 NARROWING: DOMESTIC ENTITIES AND U.S. PERSONS EXCLUDED BY REGULATION
FinCEN's implementing regulation, 31 C.F.R. § 1010.380, was revised effective March 26, 2025 (an interim final rule) and that revision was made permanent by a further final rule effective August 14, 2026. As currently in effect, the regulatory definition of "reporting company" at 31 C.F.R. § 1010.380(c)(1) no longer includes any category of domestic (U.S.-formed) entity — the paragraph that formerly defined domestic reporting companies is marked "[Reserved]" — and instead defines a reporting company only as an entity formed under the law of a foreign country that is registered to do business in a State or tribal jurisdiction by such a filing. The regulation separately states that reporting companies are exempt from reporting the beneficial ownership information of any United States persons who are beneficial owners or company applicants, and that United States persons are themselves exempt from any obligation to provide beneficial ownership information with respect to a reporting company for which they are beneficial owners or company applicants. As a result, under the rule currently in effect, entities formed in the United States (including California-formed entities) are not reporting companies regardless of size, and no U.S. person is required to be reported as, or to supply information as, a beneficial owner or company applicant of any entity, including a foreign-formed reporting company.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-06]
  "(i) [Reserved] (ii) Any entity that is: (A) A corporation, limited liability company, or other entity; (B) Formed under the law of a foreign country; and (C) Registered to do business in any State or tribal jurisdiction by the filing of a document with a secretary of state or any similar office under the law of that State or Indian tribe."
  — 31 C.F.R. § 1010.380(c)(1)-(2) — Definition of reporting company (eCFR, current as of Sept. 3, 2026), 31 C.F.R. § 1010.380(c)(1) (https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-31/subtitle-B/chapter-X/part-1010/subpart-B/section-1010.380)
  "(5) Special exemptions. (i) Reporting companies are exempt from any requirement under 31 U.S.C. 5336 and this section to report the beneficial ownership information of any United States persons who are beneficial owners or company applicants. (ii) United States persons are exempt from any requirement under 31 U.S.C. 5336 and this section to provide beneficial ownership information with respect to any reporting company for which they are beneficial owners or company applicants."
  — 31 C.F.R. § 1010.380(c)(5) — Special exemptions for United States persons, 31 C.F.R. § 1010.380(c)(5) (https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-31/subtitle-B/chapter-X/part-1010/subpart-B/section-1010.380)
  "[87 FR 59591, Sept. 30, 2022, as amended at 88 FR 76997, Nov. 8, 2023; 88 FR 83504, Nov. 30, 2023; 89 FR 83783, Oct. 18, 2024; 90 FR 13697, Mar. 26, 2025; 91 FR 52528, Aug. 14, 2026]"
  — 31 C.F.R. § 1010.380 — amendment history (source credit note), 31 C.F.R. § 1010.380, Source Credit (https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-31/subtitle-B/chapter-X/part-1010/subpart-B/section-1010.380)
  Known gap: The Federal Register documents for the March 26, 2025 interim final rule (90 FR 13697) and the August 14, 2026 final rule (91 FR 52528) could not be fetched directly this session — federalregister.gov, fincen.gov, and home.treasury.gov were all blocked by this environment's network egress controls, as was every law-firm secondary-source page attempted (Sidley, Morrison Foerster, BDO). The dates and Federal Register citations above are drawn from the amendment history embedded in the current eCFR text itself (an official primary source, independently confirmed twice), corroborated only in general terms by search-engine result snippets describing an August 2026 FinCEN final rule that adopted the 2025 interim rule 'without substantive changes.' No portion of the FinCEN or Federal Register rule preambles is quoted here because that text could not be independently verified against a fetched primary copy this session.

"BENEFICIAL OWNER" AND "COMPANY APPLICANT" DEFINED
31 U.S.C. § 5336(a)(3) defines a "beneficial owner," with respect to an entity, as an individual who, directly or indirectly, exercises substantial control over the entity or owns or controls not less than 25 percent of its ownership interests, subject to statutory exclusions for minor children (where a parent's or guardian's information is reported instead), nominees acting on behalf of another, employees whose control derives solely from employment status, individuals with a mere inheritance expectancy, and certain creditors. Under the current implementing regulation, however, this definition is only operative for a foreign-formed reporting company, and only as to individuals who are not United States persons, because United States persons are exempt from beneficial-owner and company-applicant reporting under 31 C.F.R. § 1010.380(c)(5).

[Verified — checked 2026-09-06]
  "(3) Beneficial owner .-The term "beneficial owner"- (A) means, with respect to an entity, an individual who, directly or indirectly, through any contract, arrangement, understanding, relationship, or otherwise- (i) exercises substantial control over the entity; or (ii) owns or controls not less than 25 percent of the ownership interests of the entity"
  — 31 U.S.C. § 5336(a)(3) — definition of "beneficial owner", 31 U.S.C. § 5336(a)(3) (https://uscode.house.gov/view.xhtml?req=granuleid:USC-prelim-title31-section5336&num=0&edition=prelim)
  Known gap: This clause quotes only the statute's core substantial-control/25-percent-ownership test; it does not restate the statutory text of each of the five listed exclusions (minor children, nominees, employees, inheritance expectancy, creditors) in full. The statutory "company applicant" definition, a related but separate term, is not separately quoted here.

REPORTING OBLIGATION AND TIMING UNDER FEDERAL LAW
31 U.S.C. § 5336(b)(1)(A) directs that, in accordance with regulations prescribed by the Secretary of the Treasury, each reporting company shall submit to FinCEN a report containing the beneficial ownership information described in the statute. FinCEN's implementing regulation sets specific deadlines keyed to the current, narrowed definition of reporting company: an entity that becomes a reporting company on or after March 26, 2025 must file an initial report within 30 calendar days of the earlier of actual or public notice of its registration to do business, and an entity that became a reporting company before that date was required to file no later than April 25, 2025. A reporting company must also file an updated report within 30 calendar days of any change to previously reported information, and a corrected report within 30 calendar days of discovering that a filed report was and remains inaccurate. This document does not address the mechanics of FinCEN's electronic filing system, which is described only on FinCEN's own website and could not be independently verified from a primary source in this session.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-06]
  "(A) In general .-In accordance with regulations prescribed by the Secretary of the Treasury, each reporting company shall submit to FinCEN a report that contains the information described in paragraph (2)."
  — 31 U.S.C. § 5336(b)(1)(A) — general reporting obligation, 31 U.S.C. § 5336(b)(1)(A) (https://uscode.house.gov/view.xhtml?req=granuleid:USC-prelim-title31-section5336&num=0&edition=prelim)
  "Any entity that becomes a reporting company on or after March 26, 2025 shall file a report within 30 calendar days of the earlier of the date on which it receives actual notice that it has been registered to do business or the date on which a secretary of state or similar office first provides public notice, such as through a publicly accessible registry, that the reporting company has been registered to do business."
  — 31 C.F.R. § 1010.380(a)(1) — timing of initial reports, 31 C.F.R. § 1010.380(a)(1) (https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-31/subtitle-B/chapter-X/part-1010/subpart-B/section-1010.380)
  Known gap: FinCEN's BOI E-Filing System interface and step-by-step filing instructions are published only on fincen.gov, which was unreachable from this research environment; the filing deadlines above come from the regulatory text itself (31 C.F.R. § 1010.380(a)), not from fincen.gov guidance.

ACKNOWLEDGMENT
Jordan T. Reyes, on behalf of Acme, Inc., a stock corporation formed under the law of Delaware, acknowledges having reviewed this information sheet regarding federal beneficial ownership information reporting under the Corporate Transparency Act, and understands that whether Acme, Inc. currently has any obligation under 31 U.S.C. § 5336 depends on facts about its jurisdiction of formation and the citizenship or residency of its owners that are not addressed by this sheet. Signed: _______________________ Date: September 1, 2026 Oakland, California
